key_insight: A two-color temperature-sensitive paint can directly map the cryogenic temperature field around a liquid-nitrogen three-phase contact line, revealing a local temperature dip at the interface.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical diagnostic tool for understanding and improving heat transfer in cryogenic cooling, superconducting, and space-propulsion systems.
method: Applied 2C-TSP with a temperature-sensitive dye plus a reference dye in one coating.
Used luminescence intensity ratios to compensate for optical distortions near the liquid-gas interface.
Measured temperature fields under three heat-flux conditions: 110, 430, and 900 W/m².
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a localized temperature minimum at the observed three-phase contact line, nearly constant liquid-region temperature, and increasing gas-region temperature with higher heat flux.
watch_item: Accuracy may still be affected by calibration and optical effects at extremely low temperatures and near refractive/reflective interfaces.
paper_title: Temperature distribution measurement on three-phase contact line in liquid nitrogen using two-color temperature-sensitive paint
